### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**24** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `29b4cb91e9d31281ca4e67ed1197737467515a3a` — the merge of head `b1f06284dc614f299377ceb493c2cb7a6bb4ed0e` into base `98f640d581339769d54cf27c8f7b02cbc46849f4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 29b4cb91e9d31281ca4e67ed1197737467515a3a && git checkout 29b4cb91e9d31281ca4e67ed1197737467515a3a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b1f06284dc614f299377ceb493c2cb7a6bb4ed0e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/orchestrate.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/prompts.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/scorecard.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/units.test.ts + packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/app.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/project.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/observe.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/schema.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/loader.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-run-grade.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-operation-grade.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/README.md, docs/qa/scenarios/README.md, docs/qa/scenarios/*.json (all nine cards)

Inputs: card #30882 (body and all three comments, read as claims), PR #30903 body, labels (`size/m`, `tests`, `skip-changeset`) and file list, `git diff origin/main...b1f06284` (merge base `98f640d581`, 5 files, +380/-36, three commits), the files above at `origin/main` and at the head, and the head's check-runs. The dev reports and the seat claim were checked against the tree, not adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

**Defect 1, asks 1 and 2 — a user-handle field carries a user id in the row and in `owner_id`.** The seed loop (`orchestrate.ts` `runHalf`) now, for every direct scope field holding a string, maps the handle to a persona account and sets `owner_id` as before; when the field is in `userHandleFields(card)` it also writes `body[field] = userId` and `body.owner_id = userId`, with `userId` the persona's user or `app.adminUserId()` for a handle no persona holds, and records the unheld handle in `seed.handlesAsAdmin`. Read against the crm card: ac1 and ac3 (`u_sam`) carry the sdr user in `owner` and `owner_id`, ac2 (`u_tia`) carries the admin in both; the five contacts reference loaded accounts. Against a build that models `owner` as a user lookup, 8/8 load. Verified by reading, and the `UserLookupApp` pin asserts it.

**`userHandleFields` across the nine cards.** The rule: a direct (non-path) persona scope field, not `id`, not in `expect.lookups`, not in `expect.selectFields`. I evaluated it by hand against every card at `origin/main`:
- asset_lifecycle: custodian / employee / reported_by / requested_by / department are all declared lookups, `department.id` is id. None. Values such as `e06` stay verbatim.
- crm_account_with_contacts: `account.owner` (values `u_sam`, `u_tia`). Selected.
- invoice_with_line_items: `invoice.owner` (values `u_ana` x2, `u_ben` x1; `u_ben` unheld, loads as admin). Selected.
- leave_balances: employee / department fields are lookups. None.
- order_to_cash: `account.owner` and `sales_order.owner` are declared lookups to employee (`e03` is a seeded row). None, correctly.
- project_with_tasks: `task.assignee` (values `u_kim` x3, `u_lee` x3; `u_lee` unheld). Selected.
- requisition_to_receipt: requester is a lookup, `department.id` is id. None.
- service_desk: assignee / group / customer are lookups, `customer.id` is id, `ticket_comment.visibility` is a select (`public`). None; the units test pins this card at the empty set.
- travel_expense: traveler / claimant are lookups, `department.id` is id. None.
So the selection is exactly `account.owner`, `invoice.owner`, `task.assignee`, as the PR body says; it catches every field whose seed values are person handles and leaves every row id and option value alone. No card has a truth grouped or filtered on one of those three fields, no card hides one of them (so `hiddenValues` is unaffected), and the only operations that name a handle (`project_with_tasks` `add_task` / `task_without_title`, `values.assignee: u_kim`) do so in `op.values`, which neither `operationPrompt` nor the operation grader reads (the grader reads post-state `where` / `values` only, and those do not name the assignee). The rule is correct for the library as it stands; its nature as an undeclared heuristic is noted under ④.

**Unheld handle to admin.** The card's ask 2 offers two branches: provision a non-login user, or state another contract in the build prompt. The PR takes the second and states it: the Row ownership paragraph now reads, for crm, that in `democrm_account.owner` the handle text is never stored, the runner loads the field and `owner_id` with the user's id, `u_sam` to the `sdr` user, and `u_tia`, which no person below holds, to the admin user the runner signs in as, and asks the build to make the field accept a user id with a rule on it matching that user. I compared this sentence with the seed loop line by line: field and `owner_id` both get the id; held handle gives the persona's user; unheld gives the admin. It matches. The cost the PR names (two unheld handles collapse to one user) is real but bites no card today: invoice has one unheld (`u_ben`), project one (`u_lee`), crm one (`u_tia`), and no truth groups by those fields. Honest and stated.

**Defect 1, ask 3 — a refused seed row makes the Run half not measured.** `seedDependence(card, refused)` builds the out set: the refused rows plus, to a fixed point, every seed row whose declared lookup names an out row. A question is not measured when any seed row of its object is out; an operation when its `target`, a lookup value in its `values`, or an applied post-state row (`id`, or a lookup value in its `values`) is out. `runHalf` pushes such turns with `notMeasured` and does not call the driver. `askTally` / `opsTally` count only measured turns in `passed` and `total` and carry `notMeasured`; `seedTally` renders `N/M ⚠ seed: K refused`; `verdictOf` gives `not-run` on `total === 0`, so a half with nothing measured never reads `fail`, and the run record's `notes` carries the `· N not measured` suffix. The CLI prints `renderScorecard`, so the Seed rows reach the operator.
- Can a turn that depends on a refused row still be graded? I looked for a path: truths and persona scopes traverse only lookups declared in `expect.lookups` (the loader's `checkPath`), and the closure walks exactly those, so a question whose truth reads a refused row through a path has an out row on its own object and is dropped. An operation whose post-state `where` (not `values`) names a lookup value is the one shape not inspected; in every card the same lookup is also in `op.values`, which is inspected. No false grade found.
- Can a turn that does not depend on one be wrongly dropped? Yes, by design: the question rule is object-level. On crm, a refused ct4 (account null) drops `contacts_per_account/sdr`, whose scope `account.owner = u_sam` never reads ct4. The PR body states this. It never produces a false verdict, and the cell shows the count, so it is a should-fix (④), not a must-fix.
- Not asking the dropped turns: the card says "mark ... as not measured"; a turn with no grade and no model call is the strictest reading of that and costs nothing the card asks for. Acceptable.

**Defect 2 — both author loops name the scored verify invocation.** `verifyArgs(card) = ['verify', ...verifyFlags(card)]`; `buildHalf` runs `ops.os(dir, verifyArgs(scenario.card))` and `project.ts` `os()` spawns `npx objectstack ...args`. `authoringChecks(card)` renders `npx objectstack validate`, `npx objectstack build` and `npx objectstack ${verifyArgs(card).join(' ')}`, and both `buildPreamble` and `iteratePrompt` embed it. For the iterate pass `buildHalf` receives `iteratedScenario`, which changes only `expect`, so `verifyFlags` (read from `capabilities`) is the same list the prompt named. Exact match. `templateIteratePrompt` is unchanged and names no verify; template mode runs none, so there is nothing to name.

**Tests.** Reverting each fix reds its pin: deleting `body[k] = userId` makes `UserLookupApp` refuse `u_sam` (the 8-row pin reads `refused: []`); restoring the old preamble reds the verbatim verify pin; passing an empty refused list to `seedDependence` leaves nine turns asked and graded (the `ScriptedDriver` answers from the loader's truth, so they pass, and `total: 4` / `notMeasured: 5` fail); dropping the `⚠ seed` suffix reds both scorecard string pins. The `RefusingApp` second case (all three accounts refused) pins the transitive closure without the double cascading, `not-run` on run-ask and `pass` on the one measured operation. The units test pins `seedDependence` per operation and question, including `move_eli` (target ct5 under ac3, out through the account it writes). Doubles: `UserLookupApp` refuses an `owner` or `owner_id` naming no known user on `democrm_account` and a `contact.account` naming no loaded account, with the first run's `VALIDATION_FAILED` wording; it learns persona user ids from `createPersona`. That is at least as strict as the live door for `owner` and faithful to the cascade the card recorded. The `dataContract` sentence is pinned verbatim, as the card's "must match" requires.

**The landing.** `@objectstack/scenarios` is `private: true` with no build step, so `skip-changeset` is right and nothing publishes. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct: no spec, no authorable key, no governed path. `Fixes #30882`: ask 1 (field carries the id), ask 2 (contract stated and the prompt matches the code), ask 3 (not measured, `⚠ seed: N refused`, dependents marked) and Defect 2 (verify named in both loops) are each met in the tree, so Fixes is honest for the asks; the card's Verification step (a live re-run of crm) is a model run the epic seat holds the recording for and is not performed here, which the PR says plainly. The PR body matches the tree at every claim I could check against the diff (the field selection, the three sentences, the test names and assertions, the acceptance notes). Files: five, all under `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/` and `test/runner/`; `loader.ts`, the nine card JSONs, `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` and `refusals.test.ts` are untouched, as the #30846 constraint requires. Draft: yes (the seat lands).

**Check-runs on the head (all `completed`).** Required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Test Core` success (planner produced six shards, 1/8 to 6/8 all success), `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Test UI` success, `Live E2E UI` success; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` skipped by path filter (no `ui/` change). Also green: Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards, Check PR Size. Nothing in progress.

### ② Semver level

None. The package is private and unpublished; `skip-changeset` is correct. No published package moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed surface: none touched. Tier: none; the review was asked at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER by the dispatch.
- Spec / ADR: none. QA tooling only; `packages/spec` carries no obligation for the card format.
- Serial constraint #30846: respected (see above).
- Prime Directive #10: the dev's out-of-scope finding (`personaHandles` maps every direct scope string to a persona, so on service_desk 237 public `ticket_comment` rows get `owner_id` of the portal_customer user, and rows naming two personas take the last field read) is a reproducible runner defect reported only in a comment. It needs a card (should-fix S3).

### ④ Design judgment

- S1 (should-fix). The object-level question rule in `seedDependence` drops turns that do not depend on the refused row (crm: ct4 refused takes out `contacts_per_account/sdr`, whose scope never reads ct4). The loader's truth evaluator can decide dependence exactly: a question depends on the out set when its truth, or any persona truth, differs when evaluated over the seed minus the out rows. That keeps the "never a false fail" property and measures more. Follow-up, not this PR; the cell shows the count so the loss is visible.
- S2 (should-fix). `userHandleFields` is a heuristic the card format does not declare: a future card with a direct scope on an undeclared text or option field would have that field sent as a user id and refused, with nothing at authoring to say why. Contract-first (the card is the producer) says the card should declare its user-handle fields and the loader should refuse a direct scope value on an undeclared non-lookup field that is not a handle. `loader.ts` is out of bounds for this PR; file it behind #30846. Meanwhile, recording the selected fields in the run record (beside `handlesAsAdmin`) would make a misfire readable in the record rather than only in the refusals.
- S3 (should-fix). File the `personaHandles` over-matching finding as a devx card (PD #10), naming service_desk `ticket_comment.visibility = public` and the two-persona rows as the repro; do not leave it in the report comment.
- S4 (should-fix). The card's Verification (re-run `--only crm_account_with_contacts --modes scratch`, seed 8/8) remains owed to the epic seat; the seat should say so on the card at landing so a closed card does not read as a measured re-run.
- S5 (nit). `buildHalf`'s comment says "the invocation every authoring prompt names"; the template iterate prompt names none. The package README's persona-contract line now understates the seed (it says the row is owned by the persona's user, not that the field carries the id); it is held by #30846 and should be corrected in its wake.

No must-fix. The tree does what the card's four asks say, the prompt matches the code word for word, the tests pin each ask and go red when its fix is reverted, and the half with nothing measured is `not-run` from `verdictOf` through the scorecard and the run record.

**VERDICT: PASS**
